hints: Count horizontal squares for one full sine wave from a repeating point, such as peak to next peak, noting each square is $1 \text{ cm}$ wide.
Multiply that $4 \text{ cm}$ length by the time-base $2.5 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ to get the period $T$ in $\text{ms}$.
Use $f = 1/T$ with $T$ converted to seconds to find the frequency in $\text{Hz}$.
walkthrough: Identify one complete cycle on the CRO trace. From one peak to the next peak is $4$ squares, and each square is $1 \text{ cm}$, so wavelength on screen is $4 \text{ cm}$.
State the rule: horizontal distance x time-base = time. Period $T = \text{length} \times \text{time-base}$.
Substitute values with units: $T = 4 \text{ cm} \times 2.5 \text{ ms cm}^{-1} = 10 \text{ ms}$.
Use $f = 1/T = 1/0.010 = 100 \text{ Hz}$. This is option B.
